## Summary

Pro-Vision is a Byron Center, Michigan, maker of mobile video and safety systems for commercial fleets, public safety and transit, and says it has engineered such products since 2003 [2]. The IEEE registry lists one MA-L block under this name at the same Byron Commerce Drive address the company gives [1][2]. Its hardware line covers cameras, Birdseye 360 AI, radar and sensors, the Ranger DVR, a fleet dash cam, monitors and the BodyCam 4 body-worn camera, with CloudConnect and SecuraMax software and a school-bus bundle [2].

A MAC in the Pro-Vision block is most likely a vehicle recorder or a body camera in a law-enforcement, school-transportation, transit or commercial fleet vehicle [2]. The Ranger mobile DVR lists password-protected DVR Wi-Fi, an optional 4G modem and a GPS receiver [3]. BodyCam 4 uploads through docking stations straight to SecuraMax Cloud or remotely over 4G, embeds GPS coordinates in its video and stores 64 GB on AES-256 encrypted, non-removable storage [4].

The founding year is not stated (the company says only that it has operated since 2003), and the Wi-Fi band and generation, silicon, FCC grantee codes, randomization and security history are not documented in the sources consulted: the FCC ID databases refused requests from the session that wrote this entry, and nothing is filled in from memory [2][3].
